display_name: AI-content labelling across three authorities: EU AI Act Art. 50 (with the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content), Washington E2SHB 1170 (2026), and California's AI Transparency Act as amended by SB 1000 (2026)
citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Arts 3, 50, 111(4) (as added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) and 113; Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (final, 10 June 2026); Washington Engrossed Second Substitute House Bill 1170, Chapter 167, Laws of 2026; California Business and Professions Code ss. 22757.1-22757.6, as amended by AB 853 (Stats. 2025, ch. 674) and SB 1000 (2025-2026 Reg. Sess., approved 30 September 2026)
authority: Three enacting authorities, which is why this subject is not filed under any one of them: the European Parliament and Council (the AI Act and Regulation 2026/1744); the European Commission's AI Office, facilitating a voluntary code under Art. 50(7) (the Code of Practice); the Washington State Legislature (E2SHB 1170); the California Legislature (Bus. & Prof. Code ch. 25). See README.md for the layout proposal this subject carries.
extent: EU (Art. 50 applies to providers placing systems on the Union market and to deployers in the Union); US-WA; US-CA

instruments.in_force: Art. 50 applies from 2026-08-02 (Art. 113); legacy systems have until 2026-12-02 for Art. 50(2) (Art. 111(4))
final 2026-06-10; voluntary; confirmed adequate by the Commission and the AI Board

instruments.short: Bus. & Prof. Code ch. 25 as amended by SB 1000
instruments.in_force: chapter operative 2026-08-02 (22757.6); SB 1000 text from 2026-09-30 (urgency statute); 22757.3.1 operative 2027-01-01

source.note: Every source file is deposited in source/ with its URL, fetch date and sha256 in source/sources.json; source/text/ holds mechanical plain-text extractions for quoting. The AI Act and Regulation 2026/1744 were fetched from the Publications Office cellar because eur-lex.europa.eu served a bot-challenge page on 2026-10-01. California SB 1000 was read in its enrolled form, which is the text approved on 2026-09-30; leginfo showed no chapter number on 2026-10-01. The Commission's Guidelines C(2026) 5054 are deposited as an interpretive aid and are not law.

why_this_subject: C2PA Content Credentials (signed provenance manifests) are the de facto machine-readable marking these laws reach for, yet only Washington names C2PA, and the three regimes give different answers for the same manifest. This subject encodes the three side by side so that one piece of content -- including real signed C2PA files -- can be run through all of them, and publishes where they disagree. Prompted by a suggestion to Meng Wong that L4 formalisations might fit the C2PA model; the position is in legalese/l4-pitch, Deep Dive: C2PA and Content Credentials.
